description:
Split from JMAP-x2gd.99. The burn-on-read canary test is already implemented (it exercises the message.rs:858 redaction site through a fault-injected expire_message via InjectableBackend in tests/common/mod.rs).

The duplicate-Direct cleanup test (chat.rs:363 redaction site) requires more harness than fault-injection alone: triggering the race-detection cleanup branch needs the handler to (a) pre-fetch and see NO duplicate, (b) create the new chat, (c) re-fetch and see a duplicate, (d) destroy the new chat (the lex-larger one). In sequential test calls, the handler's pre-fetch always sees existing chats, so the duplicate is intercepted at the pre-check before create_object runs. To exercise the cleanup-destroy site:

Option A: Add a 'RaceDuplicateBackend' wrapper that overrides get_objects::<Chat> with a call-counter: 1st call returns empty (so pre-fetch sees no duplicate); 2nd call returns [phantom-lex-smaller-chat, new-chat] (so race detection fires). Then inject destroy failure.

Option B: Have InjectableBackend's create_object::<Chat> ALSO insert a phantom Direct chat with a lex-smaller id in the same call. The race-detection re-fetch then sees 2 chats, picks the phantom as canonical, tries to destroy the new one.

Option B is simpler harness-wise but Option A is more focused. Either way it's ~50-80 more lines of wrapper code on top of the InjectableBackend that landed under .99.

Priority remains P3 (regression guard, not live defect). The redaction-discipline mechanism is already test-pinned at the workspace level via mail-server's ~115 canary sites.
title: Add chat-server canary test for duplicate-Direct cleanup destroy failure (split from JMAP-x2gd.99)
